author: JA
premise: A widowed baronet's second daughter is courted simultaneously by a rich, tedious neighbour and a clever but poor curate. Her elder sister, who has no suitors at all, gives her advice so evidently self-interested that the younger is driven to prefer whichever man her sister dislikes.

author: JA
premise: A family accustomed to comfort learn that their father has lost a third of his income in a failed canal investment. The mother insists on keeping the carriage for appearance's sake; the eldest daughter quietly calculates how many economies would be needed to keep it, and which of her sisters will notice.

author: JA
premise: A young woman who prides herself on her judgement is asked by her godmother to choose a husband for her cousin from among three local gentlemen. She makes her choice with care, presents it with confidence, and learns that her cousin has already accepted a fourth man nobody had thought to consider.

author: JA
premise: A sensible young woman is mortified when her mother announces at a dinner party that her daughter will soon be engaged to a gentleman who has never proposed. The gentleman is present. The daughter must undo the damage without contradicting her mother in public.
setting: A house in a country town in Hertfordshire, 1800s

author: JA
premise: A country girl visiting London for the first time with a fashionable aunt is taken up by a set of fine young ladies whose friendship proves expensive. She discovers that the aunt's own reputation in town is less secure than it appeared from the country.
setting: A house in Upper Brook Street, London, 1810s

author: JA
premise: An heiress of twenty-five, who has refused several offers and is thought cold, is unexpectedly courted by her late brother's closest friend, a naval surgeon of no family. Her guardian is opposed. She must decide whether her caution has been wisdom or merely fear.

author: JA
premise: A spinster aunt with a modest fortune lets it be understood that she will leave her money to whichever niece shows her most attention. Three nieces compete with increasing ingenuity. The fourth, who simply likes her aunt, is suspected by the others of the deepest scheme of all.

author: JA
premise: A young lady newly come into a small fortune is advised by her married sister on every particular of dress, company, and conduct. She follows the advice dutifully for a season, finds herself universally approved and thoroughly bored, and resolves to make one decision entirely on her own.

author: JA
premise: A clergyman's family is visited by a wealthy cousin who means to choose a bride among the daughters. The youngest daughter, who is fifteen and outspoken, makes it her business to mock him. Her sisters are horrified; the cousin is unexpectedly charmed.

author: JA
premise: A young lady and her mother take lodgings in a spa town for the mother's health. The mother is not ill. The daughter discovers that her mother has come to renew acquaintance with a former suitor, now widowed, and is uncertain whether to be shocked or delighted.

author: JA
premise: A young woman agrees to act in private theatricals at a neighbour's house, though she disapproves of them. The play requires her to declare love to a man she has privately admired for a year. Rehearsals become an agony of concealment.

author: JA
premise: A gentleman who has inherited an estate encumbered with debts must marry money or sell. He courts a manufacturer's daughter whose fortune would save him, and finds that she understands his situation perfectly and has terms of her own.

author: JA
premise: A young woman who believes herself above vanity is flattered by the attentions of a fashionable gentleman visiting the neighbourhood. When she learns he has been laying a wager on her affections, she must examine how much her good sense was worth.

author: JA
premise: A widow who lives in comfortable dependence on her son's estate fears that his new wife will turn her out of the house. She exhausts herself in attentions to the daughter-in-law, who wants nothing more than to be left alone with a book.

author: JA
premise: A young man of moderate means, visiting a fashionable relation in town, falls in love with a girl he believes to be an heiress. She believes him to be rich. They are both mistaken, and both too embarrassed to say so.

author: JA
premise: A young woman learns that her closest friend's brother, whom she has privately liked for some time, has lost his money at cards and is leaving for the West Indies. Her friend begs her to say nothing that might keep him in England, where his creditors wait. She must hold her tongue at the farewell dinner.

author: JA
premise: A young man about to enter the church is offered a better living by a patron on condition that he marry the patron's plain niece. He has an understanding with a girl of no fortune. His mother urges prudence. He must choose between the living and the girl.

author: JA
premise: A clergyman's wife who delights in arranging her parishioners' lives promotes a match between the village doctor and the squire's niece. Both are polite to her and to each other. Neither has the slightest wish to marry, and they unite only in their efforts to escape her kindness.

author: JA
premise: A gentleman's daughters are invited to a ball given by a rich neighbour. Their father refuses to let them go, citing the expense of new gowns. The eldest daughter, resourceful and practical, finds a way to dress them all for nothing.

author: JA
premise: A naval officer on shore leave escorts his sister to Bath, where she meets a gentleman he despises. He must decide whether to forbid the acquaintance, knowing that his sister is of age and he has no right to command her.

author: JA
premise: A young woman who has been engaged for two years to a man waiting for preferment begins to doubt that she loves him. He is good, dull, and devoted. She must decide whether to break the engagement and face her family's displeasure.

author: JA
premise: Two sisters inherit a small house and an annuity from their godmother. The elder wishes to live quietly; the younger wishes to spend the annuity on a season in London. Their brother, who expected the inheritance himself, offers to mediate.

author: JA
premise: A young lady who takes pride in her frankness offends the neighbourhood by speaking her mind about a newly married couple. She discovers too late that the bride is the sister of the man she most wishes to please.

author: JA
premise: A mother whose ambition is to see her daughters married to titles takes them to a resort where a young lord is said to be staying. The lord proves to be an awkward boy of seventeen with a governess. The daughters must disguise their mother's disappointment from the whole resort.

author: JA
premise: A clergyman's daughter staying with a rich friend in London is taken to a fashionable assembly where she knows no one. She is rescued from solitude by an amusing elderly gentleman, and finds she has spent the evening talking to the father of the man she came to London hoping to avoid.

author: JA
premise: A young widow, comfortably independent, is courted by a younger man whose family opposes the match. She has no wish to marry again, and is surprised to find that her refusals grow less certain each time he renews his suit.

author: JA
premise: A rich old gentleman, tired of his relations' attentions, announces that he will leave his fortune to a charity. His relations are devastated. His young ward, who never wanted the fortune, is the only one who visits him in the following month.

author: JA
premise: A young man who believes himself too clever to be deceived is taken in by a charming young lady who flatters his opinions. His sister, who sees through her at once, must decide whether to warn him and risk his resentment.

author: JA
premise: A gentleman of consequence is mortified when his younger brother, a cheerful sea officer, arrives unexpectedly at a formal dinner, tells stories of shipwreck, and proposes to the eldest daughter of the house before the dessert.

author: JA
premise: A young lady accompanies her invalid aunt to a spa town and is obliged to sit with her in the pump room every morning. There she observes the comedy of the town's society with growing amusement, until a gentleman notices her observing.

author: JA
premise: A young woman who has always laughed at her elder brother's choice of friends finds that the one she mocked most has become a respected magistrate and is now courting her particular friend. She must decide whether to confess to her friend everything she has said of him.

author: JA
premise: A family of daughters is thrown into consternation by the arrival of a letter from their father's long-estranged brother, who has made a fortune abroad and proposes to visit. No one remembers what the quarrel was about, and each sister has a different theory about what he will want.

author: JA
premise: A young lady takes her sister's quiet suitor for a dull man and amuses herself at his expense. When she overhears him defend her to a gossip, she must reconsider not only him but her own cleverness.

author: JA
premise: A young woman's father, a kindly but absent-minded scholar, invites a gentleman to dinner and forgets to tell his wife. The household has nothing in the larder. The daughter must manage the evening without letting the guest suspect.

author: JA
premise: Two sisters are invited to stay with a cousin who has married into a great family. They are treated as poor relations. The younger sister is resentful; the elder observes that the cousin is not happy either.

author: JA
premise: A young woman agrees to marry an older man for his kindness and his estate, and on the eve of her wedding meets his nephew, who is everything she had once hoped for. She does not break her promise. The nephew does not ask her to.

author: JA
premise: A gentleman's only son returns from university with debts his father cannot pay. The father proposes to sell the family's best timber. His wife proposes the son marry an heiress. The son proposes nothing, and goes shooting.

author: JA
premise: A young woman who is certain that a neighbour's governess is designing to marry her employer sets out to protect him. The governess has no such design. The employer, however, has.

author: JA
premise: A family's eldest son marries a woman of fashion who despises his family's country manners. She arrives for her first visit determined to reform them. The family, determined not to be reformed, close ranks with exquisite politeness.

author: JA
premise: A young lady staying in London for the season is introduced to a gentleman whose name she recognises as that of a man her brother quarrelled with years before. She does not know the cause of the quarrel. He clearly does.

author: JA
premise: A rich young man and a poor young woman, who have been meeting secretly in a shrubbery, are discovered by her aunt. The aunt, rather than forbid the match, insists on managing it, and very nearly ruins it.

author: JA
premise: A widow with three daughters and a small jointure is courted by a wealthy merchant who has made his fortune in trade. Her neighbours think the match degrading. Her daughters think it sensible. She thinks only that he is the first man to make her laugh in years.

author: JA
premise: A young woman who believes her elder sister incapable of strong feeling is astonished to discover a packet of love letters in her sister's drawer. She must decide whether to confess what she has seen, and what she now knows of her sister.

author: JA
premise: A young woman's uncle, a retired merchant of vulgar manners and great kindness, comes to stay just as she is expecting a visit from a gentleman of rank. She is ashamed of her shame, and of her uncle, and of herself.

author: JA
premise: A country clergyman visits London to petition a bishop, and is entertained by a fashionable cousin who regards him as a curiosity. His good sense and simplicity, mocked at first, begin to win the regard of the cousin's guests.

author: JA
premise: An officer of the militia, quartered in a small town, is courted by every mother with a daughter. He prefers the one young woman who seems indifferent to him, and cannot understand why his charm fails with her.

author: JA
premise: A young woman of no fortune, companion to a rich and capricious old lady, is left a legacy in her will. The old lady's relations contest it, and accuse her of undue influence. She must defend her character without appearing to care about the money.

author: JA
premise: A gentleman who prides himself on his discernment selects a wife by careful observation of her conduct. He chooses a quiet and dutiful young woman. After the wedding, he discovers that her quietness concealed a mind far sharper than his own.

author: JA
premise: A mother who fancies herself an invalid summons her married daughter home in a crisis that proves to be a cold. The daughter's husband, who has come too, is so patient with his mother-in-law that his wife begins to suspect he enjoys it.

author: JA
premise: Two young women from a country parish attend their first public ball at a resort town. One dances every dance; the other dances none. The one who dances none is the one who receives a call the next morning.

author: JA
premise: A young woman's sister has been courted for two years by a gentleman who will not declare himself. The younger sister, impatient, resolves to make him speak. Her methods are ingenious, and very nearly drive him away.

author: JA
premise: A gentleman of good family but small income is pressed by his sisters to marry a rich widow they have chosen for him. He likes the widow and dislikes being managed. He must decide whether to marry her in spite of his sisters or refuse her because of them.

author: JA
premise: A young woman convinced that her new sister-in-law is a fortune hunter watches her closely for proof. The sister-in-law, aware of the scrutiny, behaves with perfect propriety, which only confirms the young woman's suspicion.

author: JA
premise: A family's plans for a picnic are overturned when their eccentric great-aunt insists on coming and bringing her parrot. The parrot's conversation, learned from a sea captain, makes a certain impression on the gentleman the eldest daughter hopes to impress.

author: JA
premise: A young lady staying with friends in a fashionable town is warned against a gentleman with a dangerous reputation. She finds him serious, kind, and dull. Her friends cannot account for her disappointment.

author: JA
premise: A young clergyman who has always admired a neighbour's daughter at a distance is asked by her father to advise her on her reading. Their lessons are conducted with perfect propriety, and neither of them has ever been more uncomfortable.

author: JA
premise: A young heiress is warned by her guardian that every man who courts her wants only her money. She resolves to test her suitors by pretending to have lost her fortune. Only one remains, and he is the one she likes least.

author: JA
premise: A young woman of strong opinions refuses to meet her brother's fiancée, having decided from report that she is frivolous. When illness obliges them to nurse the brother together, she discovers the fiancée's patience and her own prejudice.

author: JA
premise: A young woman's younger brother, newly returned from school, falls violently in love with a governess at a neighbouring house. His family is horrified; his sister, who likes the governess, is torn between loyalty and amusement.

author: JA
premise: A widower with two daughters takes a house in London so that they may enter society. He hates society. He finds that the only person in London he can talk to is the girls' music master, an elderly émigré who hates it too.
